title: Loading messages
lead: Three ways to get messages in, and two patterns for asking a page to wait for them. They compose: bundle what every page needs, fetch the rest.
build_eager_text: The default. import.meta.glob reads the files during compilation and inlines them — no request at runtime, nothing to configure.
build_lazy_text: Drop eager: true from the same glob and each namespace becomes its own chunk, fetched the first time a page asks for it. Both forms can sit in the same messages object.
demand_lead: Two patterns for waiting on a namespace before rendering. Below, one page uses each — reload to see both run.
load_text: A universal load may return anything, including the t function itself. Works on stable SvelteKit, no compiler flags.
remote_text: A query() called like a local function, run inside your loader — no endpoint to write, no fetch to get wrong. Needs kit.experimental.remoteFunctions and compilerOptions.experimental.async.
fetch_text: The portable option: no experimental flags, works during SSR provided the URL is absolute — there is no page to be relative to on the server.
dedupe_text: Concurrent callers for the same locale and namespace share one in-flight loader call, so a hundred simultaneous SSR requests trigger one fetch, not a hundred.
